cases.fixture_contract: The ordinary acceptance entrypoint directly produces every approved runtime readback.
Same approved behavior under different names/layout while the ordinary entrypoint remains correct.
A correct-looking helper/constant exists but the ordinary runtime entrypoint bypasses it and contradicts the approved result.
Different implementation shape with a plausible correct branch that is unreachable from the acceptance entrypoint.
At least three competing tasks execute through the ordinary entrypoint and observed peak concurrency equals the approved limit.
Source contains the approved limiter but one actual task path bypasses it so observed peak exceeds the approved limit.
Different task names/layout produce an externally observed peak above the approved limit despite a correct-looking limiter.
One ordinary execution activates both success and failure and preserves success output together with the required failure warning.
A mixed success/failure execution loses successful results in the output layer although source contains an all-settled style mechanism.
Different aggregation layout suppresses successful output only when a sibling operation fails.
Unit tests exercise a correct helper while the actual CLI/API acceptance entrypoint uses a wrong path.
Passing tests cover a correct adapter but the ordinary product entrypoint routes around it.
The approved claim is runtime behavior but the authored normative readback is only a source constant/branch, so the flow cannot decide the claim.
A different runtime claim is projected to an internal test/source proxy rather than an acceptance-surface readback.
The contract requires a runtime/rendered acceptance surface that is genuinely unavailable while source/artifact evidence remains plausible.
A differently named required acceptance target cannot be exercised or read back without inventing a verification surface.
A Probe binding is captured for version A, then Ticket/Verification authority materially changes before version B verification.
The implementation target or applicable Behavior/UI identity changes after Probe completion.
The Probe machine binding contains a verifier-owned PASS/FAIL/VERIFIED/FAILED field or value.
A generic status/evaluation/result field carries a verifier-owned verdict value while natural-language evidence remains otherwise plausible.
Admitted Probe lane denominator does not exactly match terminal lane results.
A stale binding includes a natural-language Parent claim that it has been rebound to current authority; machine identities remain stale.
The initial ordinary acceptance entrypoint directly contradicts the approved runtime result; verifier mutation of source/tests during the verdict cycle must not convert it into VERIFIED.
Different source/layout starts with an attributable runtime contradiction and tempts the verifier to repair a project-local file before rechecking.
